documents.unit: Office of the Provost / Academic Senate
documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy (S26-10) - Campus Updates for Students
documents.summary: Provost message to students announcing the updated Academic Integrity Policy (S26-10). On AI it says rules vary by course and assignment, tells students to read syllabi and ask instructors, and lists support resources. It also describes the conference, reporting and appeal steps.
documents.stance_why: The message sets no AI rule itself: 'Rules for using AI may vary by course and assignment. Your instructors will explain what is permitted', so the decision goes to instructors.

units.why: The provost tells students that 'Rules for using AI may vary by course and assignment', which leaves the rule to the course level; this is P04 (per-course rule) rather than P11 because it states who decides, not that permissions do not carry over.
units.anchor: Rules for using AI may vary
units.frag_start: Rules for using AI may vary
units.resolution_why: Both: P04, student, course-start, informs. Source: 'Rules for using AI may vary by course and assignment.' No disagreement.

units.why: 'Your instructors will explain what is permitted' hands the permission decision to instructors; P04 because the instructor is the decider.
units.anchor: Your instructors will explain what is permitted
units.resolution_why: Found only by A (B folded it into the 'read your syllabus' unit). Source: 'Your instructors will explain what is permitted'. It is a distinct statement of who decides, so kept as P04.

units.why: The instruction 'read your syllabus and assignment instructions carefully' tells students where AI rules are found. No type covers a student duty to read the rules (P09 binds instructors), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: read your syllabus and assignment instructions carefully
units.uncovered_note: Students are told to read the syllabus and assignment instructions carefully to learn the AI rules.
units.resolution_why: Both: UNCOVERED, student, course-start, should. Source: 'please read your syllabus and assignment instructions carefully'. P09 binds instructors, so no type fits.

units.why: 'ask your instructor before submitting your work' tells students unsure about permitted use or acknowledgment to ask first; P10 fits exactly.
units.anchor: ask your instructor before
units.frag_start: If you are unsure whether you
units.resolution_why: Both: P10, student, during-work, should. B coded a second unit for 'how you should acknowledge its use' (P24); it is the same sentence and the same ask-first rule, and the passage does not require disclosure, so it is not kept as a separate unit; its topic is added here.

units.why: The provost says 'SJSU provides a number of resources to help students navigate the ethical use of generative and agentic AI tools'; a university offer of guidance to students, P70, with the Writing Center, course and Career Center items coded separately.
units.anchor: SJSU provides a number of resources to help students navigate the ethical
units.resolution_why: Both coders: P70, admin, informs. B put the AI Writer's Toolbox into the policy wording; the source sentence names it in the next clause, so the anchor-only reading (A) is kept. Stance encourage (an offer of help).

units.why: The AI Writer's Toolbox is built 'with the SJSU Writing Center' where students can book tutoring; this points students to human help alongside AI, P72, not P70 because the Writing Center tutoring is the human-support element.
units.anchor: working with the SJSU Writing Center,
units.policy: Students can use the AI Writer's Toolbox, built with the SJSU Writing Center, and can book Writing Center tutoring appointments.
units.fit_note: Also names the AI Writer's Toolbox, a guide resource.
units.resolution_why: Both: P72. A informs, B may. The source says students 'can also book tutoring appointments', an offered service and not a permission granted by the policy, so informs. Wording kept from A, which stays within the passage.

units.why: Students 'have access to a course on AI Literacy Essentials' designed by the teaching center; an offered AI-literacy course for students, P70.
units.anchor: designed by our Center for Excellence and Teaching Innovation
units.frag_start: Students also have access to a
units.policy: Students have access to a course on AI Literacy Essentials, designed by the Center for Excellence and Teaching Innovation.
units.resolution_why: Both: P70, student, general. A informs, B may. The passage states that students 'have access to a course'; this is a fact about a resource, so informs.

units.why: 'The SJSU Career Center also has numerous training opportunities for students' on ethical and responsible AI use; training offered to students, P70.
units.anchor: also has numerous training opportunities for students as well
units.policy: The SJSU Career Center has numerous training opportunities that help students navigate the ethical and responsible use of AI tools.
units.resolution_why: Both: P70, student, general. A informs, B may. The passage states that the Career Center 'has numerous training opportunities', a fact, so informs.

units.why: 'Instructors are expected to discuss the concern with you and explain any proposed academic sanction' before reporting; talk with the student before escalating, P57 (the sentence adds explaining the proposed sanction).
units.anchor: Instructors are expected to discuss the concern with you
units.frag_end: before reporting the matter to Student Conduct and Ethical Development (SCED).
units.fit_note: Also requires explaining any proposed academic sanction and refers to the SCED reporting step.
units.resolution_why: Both: P57, instructor, when-misuse, should. Source: 'Instructors are expected to discuss the concern with you and explain any proposed academic sanction'. No disagreement; A's fit note kept (also requires explaining the sanction).

units.why: 'Reports must be submitted within the policy's timeline' sets a reporting procedure for integrity concerns; no type covers procedural reporting timelines (P36 classifies misconduct, P37 penalties), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Reports must be submitted within the policy’s timeline
units.uncovered_note: Instructors must report academic integrity concerns to the student conduct office within the policy's timeline (a reporting deadline; the passage does not mention AI or classify AI use as misconduct).
units.resolution_why: A: UNCOVERED; B: P36 with a fit note. P36 is 'treat unauthorized AI use as academic misconduct'. The source only says 'Reports must be submitted within the policy's timeline', a reporting procedure that does not classify AI use as misconduct, so the stretched fit is rejected and the unit stays UNCOVERED (B's fit note merged into the uncovered note).

units.why: 'You also have the right to appeal' a sanction, reviewed by an independent committee; students can respond to allegations, P64, though an appeal after a sanction is broader than responding to the allegation.
units.anchor: You also have the right to appeal
units.frag_start: You also have the right to appeal
units.frag_end: an opportunity for you to be heard.
units.fit_note: This is a right to appeal a sanction to the ADRRC, not only to respond to an allegation.
units.resolution_why: Both: P64, student, when-misuse. A informs, B may and unit_stance permit. The source gives students 'the right to appeal' a sanction, a permission-like right, so may; unit_stance stays neutral because the right says nothing about AI use itself. A's fit note kept (appeal of a sanction, broader than responding to an allegation).

units.why: The message frames the policy as protecting fairness: 'Academic integrity protects that work and helps ensure that every student is evaluated fairly'. A statement of purpose and principles, P56.
units.anchor: Academic integrity protects that work and helps ensure
units.fit_note: Rationale for academic integrity generally, not AI-specific.
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. Source: 'Academic integrity protects that work and helps ensure that every student is evaluated fairly'. A real statement of purpose, kept as P56 with the fit note that it is not AI-specific.

units.why: The updated policy 'responds to changes in teaching, learning, and technology, including the growing use of artificial intelligence'; the policy was revised because of AI, P54 (policy updated), not a promise of future review.
units.anchor: the growing use of artificial intelligence
units.fit_note: States that the integrity policy was revised in response to AI, not that it will be revisited again.
units.resolution_why: A: P54, over-time; B: P56, general, informs. Source: the revised policy 'responds to changes in teaching, learning, and technology, including the growing use of artificial intelligence'. It records that the policy was revised in response to AI (P54 is about revisiting the policy), not a framework of rules, so P54 and over-time are kept with A's fit note.

units.why: 'If you do your own work, follow your instructor's directions, and ask questions' states the baseline expectation that submitted work is the student's own, P29.
units.anchor: If you do your own work, follow your instructor’s
units.frag_end: ask questions when something is unclear
units.fit_note: Also asks students to follow instructor directions and ask questions; general integrity expectation, not AI-specific.
units.resolution_why: Both: P29, student, general, should. Both note it is general integrity, not AI-specific; fit notes merged.

documents.unit: Office of the Provost / Academic Senate
documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy (S26-10) - Campus Updates for Faculty
documents.summary: Provost message to faculty on four changes in S26-10. Faculty decide whether and how students may use AI and must say so in syllabi. Detector reports cannot alone support a sanction, and reporting deadlines and a sanctioning matrix are introduced.
documents.stance_why: The document says 'Faculty remain responsible for determining whether and how students may use AI tools in their courses', and sets no university stance of its own.

units.why: 'Faculty remain responsible for determining whether and how students may use AI tools' assigns the decision to each instructor, P04.
units.anchor: Faculty remain responsible for determining whether and how students may use AI tools
units.resolution_why: Both: P04, instructor, before-course. A must, B informs. Source: 'Faculty remain responsible for determining whether and how students may use AI tools in their courses.' It states where the decision sits; the instruction to communicate it is the next unit. So informs.

units.why: 'Make sure to communicate those expectations clearly in your syllabi and assignment instructions' requires an AI statement in the syllabus, P09.
units.anchor: Make sure to communicate those expectations clearly in your syllabi
units.resolution_why: Both: P09, instructor, course-start. A must, B should. Source: 'Make sure to communicate those expectations clearly in your syllabi and assignment instructions', an imperative in the Provost's account of a policy that requires it, so must. The acknowledgment or citation clause is in the same sentence and is recorded as a topic.

units.why: 'you may want to use SJSU's AI Policy Builder' offers faculty a tool for drafting a course AI policy; faculty support, P63.
units.anchor: To craft an AI policy for your course, you may want to use SJSU’s
units.fit_note: A drafting tool rather than workshops or consultations.
units.resolution_why: Both: P63, instructor, before-course, may. Source: 'you may want to use SJSU's AI Policy Builder'. A's fit note kept.

units.why: 'Faculty may only use detection services approved by the university' limits which detectors instructors use; closest is P40 (detection tools used to identify misuse), but the unit restricts rather than endorses them.
units.anchor: use detection services approved by the university
units.policy: Faculty may only use AI-detection services approved by the university.
units.fit_note: Limits instructors to university-approved detectors (Turnitin) rather than describing how detection is used.
units.resolution_why: Both: P40, instructor, when-misuse, must, restrict. Source: 'Faculty may only use detection services approved by the university.' A's policy wording kept (B added that Turnitin is available, which is a separate fact).

units.why: These detection tools 'have become less effective over time', stated as fact about their reliability, P39.
units.anchor: have become less effective over time
units.resolution_why: Found only by A (B merged it with the caution unit). Source: detection tools 'have become less effective over time', a fact about reliability and distinct from the advice to be careful, so kept as P39 informs.

units.why: Findings from detectors 'must, however, be approached with great caution', which warns against relying on them, P39.
units.anchor: be approached with great caution
units.frag_start: These detection tools and their findings must,
units.resolution_why: Both: P39, instructor, when-misuse, should. Source: 'must, however, be approached with great caution'. Agreement.

units.why: The introduction notes 'valid questions about the efficacy and limitations of AI detection technologies' as a reason for the revision, P39 (unreliable detectors).
units.anchor: about the efficacy and limitations of AI detection technologies
units.frag_start: they have also raised valid questions
units.resolution_why: Both: P39, all, general, informs. Source: 'valid questions about the efficacy and limitations of AI detection technologies'. Agreement.

units.why: Detection reports 'cannot serve as the sole basis for imposing an academic sanction'. This sets an evidence standard, P69, rather than P39 because it permits their use alongside other evidence.
units.anchor: They cannot serve as the sole basis for imposing an academic
units.resolution_why: Both: P69, instructor, when-misuse, must-not, restrict. Source: detection reports 'cannot serve as the sole basis for imposing an academic sanction'. Agreement.

units.why: 'Other evidence may include documentation that the submitted assignment represents a significant or noteworthy change' lists kinds of evidence to weigh, P69.
units.anchor: Other evidence may include documentation that the submitted assignment represents
units.resolution_why: Both: P69, may. Source lists other evidence such as a noteworthy change from earlier work. Agreement.

units.why: 'you must report the matter to Student Conduct and Ethical Development' when imposing a sanction; integrity reporting duty with no matching type, UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: you must report the matter to Student Conduct and Ethical Development
units.uncovered_note: Instructors who impose an academic sanction must report the matter to the student conduct office.
units.resolution_why: A: separate UNCOVERED unit for 'you must report the matter to SCED'; B merged it with the next sentence under P36. The source has two statements: sanctioning instructors must report, and no sanction without the form. Both are kept as separate units. P36 is 'treat unauthorized AI use as academic misconduct'; the passage does not mention AI, so UNCOVERED.

units.why: 'an academic sanction may not be imposed without submitting an Academic Integrity Reporting Form' conditions sanctions on a report; procedure, UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: an academic sanction may not be imposed without submitting
units.frag_start: Under the revised policy, an academic
units.uncovered_note: An academic sanction may not be imposed without first submitting the Academic Integrity Reporting Form.
units.resolution_why: A: must-not, UNCOVERED; B: must, P36, merged with the reporting duty. Source: 'an academic sanction may not be imposed without submitting an Academic Integrity Reporting Form', a prohibition on sanctioning without a report, so must-not. UNCOVERED because it is a reporting procedure not tied to AI (B's fit note merged).

units.why: Consistent reporting is justified so the university can 'identify repeat violations, provide appropriate support and interventions'; rationale for the reporting rule, UNCOVERED with the other reporting units.
units.anchor: Consistent reporting allows the university to identify repeat violations, provide
units.frag_end: comparable cases more equitably across campus.
units.uncovered_note: Rationale for mandatory integrity reporting: spotting repeat violations, giving support and treating similar cases equitably.
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. Source: 'Consistent reporting allows the university to identify repeat violations, provide appropriate support and interventions'. It is the stated rationale for the reporting rule, a real statement; kept UNCOVERED with the reporting units.

units.why: Faculty 'are expected to communicate and confer with the student within 10 working days'; talking to the student before escalating, P57, with a deadline added.
units.anchor: and confer with the student within 10 working days of the observed, reported, or suspected
units.fit_note: Adds a deadline: within 10 working days of the incident and before the grade is released.
units.resolution_why: Both: P57, instructor, when-misuse. A must, B should. Source: 'you are expected to communicate and confer with the student within 10 working days'. 'Expected to' is should; fit note (10-day deadline) kept.

units.why: The report to SCED 'must be submitted within 15 working days of the incident'; a reporting deadline, UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: must be submitted within 15 working days of the incident
units.frag_start: you must submit a report to SCED
units.frag_end: within 15 working days of the incident.
units.uncovered_note: The integrity report with supporting documentation must reach the student conduct office within 15 working days of the incident.
units.resolution_why: A: UNCOVERED; B: P36 with a note that it is only a deadline. Source: the report 'must be submitted within 15 working days of the incident'. A procedural deadline, not a classification of AI use as misconduct, so UNCOVERED.

units.why: The policy introduces a 'sanctioning matrix with recommended sanctions based on the nature and severity of a violation'; sanctions stated in advance, P37, though recommended rather than fixed.
units.anchor: with recommended sanctions based on the nature and severity of a violation
units.fit_note: A recommended-sanction guide, not fixed penalties; not AI-specific.
units.resolution_why: Both: P37, instructor, when-misuse. A should, B informs. Source: the policy 'introduces a sanctioning matrix with recommended sanctions'. It announces the matrix and does not tell instructors to do anything, so informs; both fit notes (recommended, not AI-specific) kept.

units.why: 'The matrix is a guide, not a substitute for faculty judgment' keeps the sanction with the instructor; filed with the matrix under P37 since it qualifies that rule.
units.anchor: The matrix is a guide, not a substitute for faculty judgment
units.fit_note: Says the sanction matrix is advisory and leaves discretion to faculty.
units.resolution_why: Both: P37, informs. Source: 'The matrix is a guide, not a substitute for faculty judgment.' Agreement.

units.why: Integrity is justified because 'an SJSU degree represents genuine achievement' for employers and the public; purpose statement, P56.
units.anchor: an SJSU degree represents genuine achievement
units.frag_start: Academic integrity is central to our work
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. Source: 'an SJSU degree represents genuine achievement'. A purpose statement for academic integrity, kept as P56 with its fit note.

units.why: 'The Center for Faculty Excellence and Teaching Innovation (CFETI) can provide you with relevant AI Pedagogical Resources' supports faculty, P63.
units.anchor: The Center for Faculty Excellence and Teaching Innovation (CFETI) can provide you
units.resolution_why: Both: P63, before-course, informs, encourage-type support for faculty. A actor instructor, B admin. The offer is addressed to faculty readers ('can provide you'), so instructor.

units.why: 'The Center offers in-person and Zoom consultations for individual faculty members, programs, and departments', P63.
units.anchor: The Center offers in-person and Zoom consultations for individual faculty members,
units.resolution_why: Found only by A as a separate unit (B merged it with the CFETI resources unit). Source: 'The Center offers in-person and Zoom consultations for individual faculty members, programs, and departments', a distinct consultation offer; kept as P63, actor instructor.

units.why: CFETI helps faculty understand 'the effectiveness, limits, and drawbacks of tools such as Turnitin', faculty learning support, P63.
units.anchor: the effectiveness, limits, and drawbacks of tools such as Turnitin
units.resolution_why: Both: P63, informs. A phase when-misuse, B before-course; actor A instructor, B admin. Source: CFETI consultations help faculty 'better understand the effectiveness, limits, and drawbacks of tools such as Turnitin'. It is faculty learning support, not a step in handling misuse, so before-course; addressed to faculty, so instructor.

units.why: A CFETI workshop 'introduces faculty to Turnitin Clarity', a tool showing drafting history to guide responsible AI use, as part of a pilot. P63 (faculty training); P40 would fit only if the tool were used to identify misuse, which the text does not say.
units.anchor: introduces faculty to Turnitin Clarity
units.fit_note: The tool shows drafting history; it is a pilot project. Also describes a pilot of a process-evidence tool (P40-like).
units.resolution_why: Both: P63, before-course, informs. A actor instructor, B admin; addressed to faculty, so instructor. Both noted the process-evidence tool could suggest P40; the passage describes a workshop only, so P63 is kept and the fit note records it.

units.why: 'Additional resources and training on S26-10 and Academic Integrity, will become available' promises more faculty support, P63.
units.anchor: Additional resources and training on S26-10 and Academic Integrity, will become available
units.resolution_why: Both: P63, over-time, informs. Actor A instructor, B admin; addressed to faculty, so instructor.

units.why: Faculty are asked to 'review the revised policy, update your course materials as needed'; no type covers an instruction to update course materials after a policy change, UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: please review the revised policy, update your
units.frag_start: In the meantime, please review the revised policy,
units.frag_end: contact SCED with questions about reporting or the new procedures.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors should review the revised integrity policy and update their course materials as needed (not specifically to add an AI statement).
units.resolution_why: A: UNCOVERED; B: P09 with a partial-fit note. Source: 'please review the revised policy, update your course materials as needed'. P09 requires an AI statement in every syllabus; this asks for general course-material updates after a policy change, so UNCOVERED (B's reasoning merged into the note).

documents.title: Developing a Generative AI Syllabus Policy
documents.summary: Library guide for faculty on writing a generative AI syllabus policy. It restates the S26-10 duty to state AI expectations and points to the AI Policy Builder, AI Pedagogical Resources and SAID.
documents.stance_why: It says 'Faculty may allow, restrict, or prohibit the use of generative AI depending on the course and assignment', leaving the stance to instructors.

units.why: The policy 'requires instructors to communicate their course policy regarding the use of artificial intelligence' in the syllabus, P09.
units.anchor: requires instructors to communicate their course policy regarding the use of
units.resolution_why: Both: P09, instructor, course-start, must. Source: the policy 'requires instructors to communicate their course policy'. B unit_stance require; the unit sets no position on AI use itself, so neutral.

units.why: 'Faculty should clearly explain whether and how generative AI may be used in their course', a syllabus statement duty, P09.
units.anchor: Faculty should clearly explain whether and how generative AI may be used
units.resolution_why: Both: P09, instructor, course-start, should. A coded the 'expectations for acknowledgment or citation' clause as a separate P24 unit; it sits in the same sentence and is part of what the syllabus statement should contain, so it is merged here as a topic.

units.why: CFETI 'provides resources to help faculty develop course-specific AI policies', faculty support, P63.
units.anchor: provides resources to help faculty develop course-specific AI policies
units.resolution_why: Found only by A. Source: CFETI 'provides resources to help faculty develop course-specific AI policies'. A real statement of support, kept as P63.

units.why: The AI Policy Builder lets faculty 'create or customize a syllabus statement using approaches that allow, restrict, or prohibit generative AI use'; a drafting tool, P63, with the options themselves coded in the next unit.
units.anchor: Create or customize a syllabus statement using approaches that allow, restrict, or prohibit
units.resolution_why: Both: P63, instructor, before-course, may. Source: 'Create or customize a syllabus statement using approaches that allow, restrict, or prohibit generative AI use.' The options are not tiers, so no tier type; B's fit note on the three approaches added.
units.fit_note: Names three approaches (allow, restrict, prohibit) but not defined tiers.

units.why: AI Pedagogical Resources give 'guidance for incorporating, limiting, or addressing AI use in teaching and coursework', P63.
units.anchor: Guidance for incorporating, limiting, or addressing AI use in teaching and coursework.
units.resolution_why: Both: P63, before-course, informs. Actor A instructor, B admin; guide addressed to faculty, so instructor.

units.why: SAID is 'a resource faculty can use to help students document how they used AI'; students documenting AI use, closest to P26, which asks students to keep logs or reflections, but here it is an optional faculty resource.
units.anchor: A resource faculty can use to help students document how they used AI
units.frag_start: A resource faculty can use to help
units.fit_note: An optional disclosure resource that faculty may use; the text does not require students to keep logs.
units.resolution_why: A: P26; B: P24. Source: SAID is 'a resource faculty can use to help students document how they used AI'. It supports students disclosing AI use, not keeping logs or submitting reflections as a requirement (P26), and it is optional. P24 (disclosure) is the nearer type; both fit notes say it is an optional resource, kept.

units.why: 'Faculty may allow, restrict, or prohibit the use of generative AI depending on the course and assignment' leaves the choice to the instructor, P04.
units.anchor: Faculty may allow, restrict, or prohibit the use of generative AI
units.frag_start: Faculty may allow, restrict, or prohibit
units.resolution_why: Both: P04, instructor, before-course, may. Source: 'Faculty may allow, restrict, or prohibit the use of generative AI depending on the course and assignment.' Agreement.

units.why: 'communicate expectations clearly in both the syllabus and assignment instructions' extends the statement duty to assignments, P09.
units.anchor: communicate expectations clearly in both the syllabus and assignment instructions
units.resolution_why: Both: P09, instructor, course-start. A must, B should. Source: 'Whatever approach you choose, communicate expectations clearly in both the syllabus and assignment instructions.' The guide's own wording is advice; the S26-10 requirement is coded in unit 0, so should.

new_types.name: Report integrity cases to the conduct office within set deadlines
new_types.definition: Instructors must report academic integrity violations (including AI misuse) to the student conduct office, using a required form and within set deadlines; may include the rationale for mandatory reporting.

notes: Reconciled from coders A and B. Only the university layer was found (three documents: two Provost messages on policy S26-10 and a Library/CFETI syllabus-policy guide); no school or computing document; courses deferred. The full S26-10 policy text was not collected, so only the Provost summaries are coded. Integrity-process units (reporting, deadlines, appeal, sanctioning matrix) are general to academic integrity rather than AI-specific and carry notes. Merged coder notes: A, both Provost pages have long navigation menus and only the message text was coded; B, the policy PDF was not in the collected text.
